No fixed retry count; only the total deadline and cumulative drive budget bound it. Protective stops stay terminal: body proximity, stale/reordered scans or clocks, bridge lock/link loss, deadlines, feedback mismatch.

A new identity whose first sighting lies within .30 m (tracker association gate) of the last full sighting, seen within .60 s, is re-bound once it confirms. Resume still needs the confirmed, fully isolated orbit support. Orbit target loss/identity change now enters this wait instead of a terminal coast.
change.repeatable_pauses: Left-turn pause and orbit wait are no longer single-use (recovery_count reported).
change.post_pass_pause: After the first pass, quality faults (scan_incomplete / bounded front_sparse) pause at neutral holding the ACKed command (right allowed, 1350..1720) instead of halting; resume in the same stage when quality is clean and the stage input is observed again.
change.recovery_hold: After the first pass, exit/corridor losses beyond their lease (missing, ambiguous, identity change, invalid), exit budget, corridor body-margin rule, light-stage budget and missing free space enter a neutral recovery hold. change.second_target_loss: Second-target loss or second-entry timeout returns to corridor_follow (re-acquires), instead of a terminal coast.
change.server: post-pass pause branch; motion-initiated waits/holds detected (drive -> quality_wait) and given fresh neutral/resume sequences; eligibility accepts held right commands for post-pass pauses/recovery holds and a pending neutral while the bridge still reports 1550.

runs.7 straight 1560 2.5 s: starts ~.4 s after the command, ~.6 m/s at 1 s, 1.5 m/s at 2 s, ~2.0-2.4 m/s at 2.6 s (ICP speeds noisy); at servo 1500 it curved RIGHT about -.17 /m throughout (centre moved after the repair); after the stop ~2.0 m/s held for ~.5 s, then about .6 m/s^2; >3.2 m after the stop and still ~1 m/s when the 1.8 s coast log ended
runs.8 right 1400 (1550): turn about -.13 /m (inside the deadband, same as the 1500 right drift); centre -.15..-.2 /m; guard stopped it at the end (front-right post)
runs.9 right 1300 (1550): turn -.35..-.42 /m; after 1500 -.2..-.33 /m decaying to about -.15 /m, still right after the stop
runs.10 left 1720 1.1 s (1550): only ~.4 s of motion in the turn phase (about +.6 /m while ramping, ICP glitches); after 1500 it kept about +.25 /m LEFT for >1 s, also after the stop

conclusions: After the repair the large right turn returns like the left one (~.25 s lag, no lasting residual); a 1585/.2 s kick is not needed and over-corrects.

A centre deadband now exists: right 1350 hardly turns (left deadband to 1580 per user); the 160 PWM per 1/m linear model is invalid near centre; right 1200 about 1.3 /m, left 1720 about 1.6 /m (before repair).
Next: fit a deadband + gain model from cleaner runs (left 1600/1650/1720, right 1400/1300/1200), then update ROUTE_PWM_PER_CURVATURE use, RIGHT_EXIT_MIN_PWM and the simulator.
additional_conclusions: Throttle lags the command both ways by ~.4-.7 s (start and stop); the bridge sends 1500 every 20 ms after stop (vehicle-bridge.rs), so the lag is in the ESC/chassis (ramp or neutral setting). Coast after that ~.6-.8 m/s^2 on tile. The simulator has neither the lag nor 2 m/s at 1560.
After the repair 1500 is not straight: about -.17 /m right at 1560; the left deadband readings are relative to this bias (1600 ~ +.27, 1650 ~ +.57 /m relative to 1500).
Recommend: check the ESC programming (drag/neutral brake, throttle ramp/punch); re-trim the steering centre; measure 1580/1600 only with >= 8 m clear or outdoors.

steering_table_after_repair.units: 1/m at about .6 m/s on tile; ICP noise about +-.1 /m

steering_arc_after_repair_20261016.final_conclusion: The 1500 drift is not a fixed bias but backlash: after a right turn 1500 keeps about -.2 /m, after a left turn about +.25 /m (operator: structural). Deadband about 1350..1590. Model for the route and simulator: wheel follows the servo with play of roughly +-100 PWM, then a steep gain outside it. Software compensation is now justified by data: jump across the play when the steering direction changes, then the measured gain; fit and validate in simulation before any route change.

At ~2 m/s that is about 3-3.5 m, at ~1.4 m/s about 2 m. 1560 is a power level, not a speed: speed keeps rising for >2 s (1.2 -> 1.9 m/s). analysis.conclusion: the calibration fixed how much a command turns (start lane steady) but not how fast the steering changes: the loop pursuits assume an instant steering change while a full reversal takes ~1-2 s at ~1-1.5 m/s.
